subject: Dedicated capacity validation — GPU matrix & next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@notablehealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity validation — GPU matrix & next steps

Hi Emma — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we book validation runs.

Call recap (high level)
- Goal: validate Dedicated capacity sizing for Notable Health’s chat & summarization workloads so you can commit to reserved capacity with predictable latency/cost.
- Primary SLOs you called out: 95th latency <= 300ms for short chat responses (<=64 tokens) in streaming mode, and end-to-end 95th <= 1.2s for long summaries (~512 tokens).
- Throughput/concurrency targets: support peak of ~200 concurrent users (typical message sizes skew short) and sustained aggregate throughput ~1,200 tokens/s during peak windows.
- Streaming behavior: partials every ~150ms is desired (low inter-token jitter), and graceful degraded tail behavior when concurrency spikes.

What Redwood will validate (proposed)
- GPU profiles: H100 80GB (baseline perf), A100 80GB (FP16), and an L4-like low-cost variant for cost tradeoffs.
- Workloads: replay of your provided prompt sample (thanks in advance), plus synthetic tail bursts to test autoscaling & prefix/KV cache effects.
- Metrics we’ll produce: p50/p95/p99 latency (partial and final), tokens/sec, GPU utilization, memory headroom, KV hit rate, and cost-per-1M tokens estimate for each profile.

Action items / proposed schedule
1) You: please send the prompt sample and 24h peak window examples (user mix + concurrency).
2) Redwood (Rafael + infra): run a controlled validation across the three GPU profiles, produce a GPU matrix CSV and an executive summary.
3) Joint call to review results and pick reserved throughput+commit level (canary -> full rollout).

Attachments: I’ve attached a short validation plan and a template matrix we’ll populate (dedicated-validation-plan.pdf, gpu-benchmark-matrix.csv).

Open questions for you (short)
- Are there any content-safety model variants you require us to include in the baseline?
- Any hard guardrails on maximum acceptable cost per 1M tokens?

If that looks right I’ll ask Rafael to schedule the runs for next Tue/Wed and share the exact test window.

Thanks,
Olga
--
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@notablehealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@notablehealth.com
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity validation — GPU matrix & next steps

Thanks Olga — this is great and captures our needs. A few clarifications and attachments below.

Clarifications
- SLOs: we can accept p95 <= 350ms for streaming partials if final assembly p95 stays <= 1s for short flows, but prefer you to target <=300ms if possible.
- Concurrency: the 200 concurrent users is our peak for a single region; global peak could hit 300 but we expect regional sharding.
- Prompt mix: ~70% chat (<=64 tokens), 25% short summaries (65-256 tokens), 5% long summaries (~512 tokens).
- Safety: yes, we require the content-safety variant (light filter) in the baseline. If performance delta is material we can evaluate tradeoffs.

Attached: notable-prompt-sample.jsonl (5k rows compressed) contains representative prompts and a small telemetry snapshot from last week with time-of-day distribution.

We’re flexible on the test window — prefer Tue/Wed as you suggested. Please send a narrow window (2-3 hour) for the controlled run and we’ll try to stop any internal scheduled jobs during that period.

Best,
Emma
--
Emma Liu
Head of Platform, Notable Health
emma.liu@notablehealth.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@notablehealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity validation — GPU matrix & next steps

Emma — perfect, thanks for the sample and the extra context. Rafael / Marissa — FYI I’ve attached Notable’s prompt set and their stated SLOs. Can we confirm available windows next Tue (2026-02-17) 09:00–12:00 PT or Wed 09:00–12:00 PT for the controlled runs? I propose we run three 30–45 minute validation passes (one per GPU profile) with a short cool-down between runs to collect steady-state metrics.

Proposed test plan (short):
- Replay real prompt set at production concurrency shape, with two synthetic spike events (2x and 3x) to stress tails.
- Streaming mode enabled; measure partial delivery intervals and p95 final assembly latency.
- Capture KV cache hit/miss profile by varying prefix distributions.
- Compare H100 / A100 / L4 profiles on the same model artifact (quantized when appropriate) and report cost-per-1M tokens.

I’ll schedule the calendar hold once you confirm the preferred day. Rafael — can you confirm infra reservations and whether we should use dedicated instances or ephemeral capacity for the A100 test? Also please populate the gpu-benchmark-matrix.csv with the fields you’ll report.

Thanks,
Olga
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity validation — GPU matrix & next steps

Olga / Marissa — confirmed for Tue 2026-02-17 09:00–12:00 PT (we’ll reserve the window and the infra). Quick operational notes and what I’ll run: 

Run plan (ops)
- Reserve: Dedicated nodes for H100 (2x reserved for redundancy), A100 as reserved nodes if cost approved (we’ll use 1x reserved + 1x ephemeral), L4 profile on ephemeral fleet to approximate low-cost variant.
- Model artifact: we’ll use the same model version you specified, with FP16 + 4-bit quant for L4 where supported (will log exact quant config).
- Load: replay notable-prompt-sample.jsonl at the provided concurrency curve. We’ll run three passes (~40m each) with 15m cool-down intervals.
- Observability: export p50/p95/p99, partial delivery intervals, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory headroom, KV hit rate, and per-run cost estimate. We’ll push raw metrics to the shared Drive link and a summary CSV (gpu-benchmark-matrix.csv).

Risks / notes
- If we see memory pressure on the A100 config for long summaries, we may need to reduce batch sizes or enable offloading — we’ll document any config changes.
- Streaming partial interval measurement requires precise client-side clock alignment; I’ll include a small client harness that emits timestamps to validate sub-100ms jitter.

I’ll attach the matrix template populated with the exact columns we’ll publish. Once runs complete I’ll send the filled CSV + an exec summary and proposed reserved throughput recommendation (tokens/sec + concurrency + commit band).

Rafael
--
Rafael Mendes
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
